direct_answer:
Galp integrates sustainability-related performance into its performance evaluation framework through ESG criteria that are directly linked to annual variable remuneration for both employees and the Executive Committee [Source 1]. For employees, ESG metrics account for 25% of total remuneration [Source 1]. For the Executive Committee, ESG metrics represent 25% of the quantitative performance-based remuneration component (which is 65% of remuneration), and this proportion can increase further based on achievement of strategic objectives [Source 1].

The ESG-linked KPIs/targets used include: (i) Energy transition (15% weighting): absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions and sales carbon intensity; (ii) Safety (10%): Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR); and (iii) Strategy execution (10%): completion of strategic milestones including execution of low carbon projects and renewable energy generation portfolio, cyber risk reduction, and employee engagement index improvement [Source 1]. Performance in these KPIs is assessed using values outlined in business plans approved by the Board of Directors, and results are evaluated against actual performance at the end of each period [Source 1].

For long-term incentives, members of the Executive Committee have a specific long-term incentive in the form of Galp shares vesting after four years; the number of shares effectively attributed is based on three categories, including reduction of sales carbon intensity [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: The passages describe key characteristics of the incentive schemes (annual variable remuneration and a long-term share-based incentive for the Executive Committee) and specify sustainability-related targets/metrics (Scope 1&2 emissions, sales carbon intensity, TRIR, and strategic milestones including low-carbon projects) and their weightings [Source 1]. They also identify that KPI values come from business plans approved by the Board of Directors, indicating the approval level for performance benchmarks [Source 1]. However, the disclosure does not fully cover all ESRS 2 GOV-3 elements for administrative, management and supervisory bodies (e.g., it does not explicitly address supervisory body remuneration, nor clearly state the proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability targets for the Executive Committee as a share of total variable/total remuneration, nor the governance level for approving/updating incentive scheme terms) [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Explicit coverage of sustainability-linked incentives/remuneration for the supervisory body (and broader administrative/management/supervisory bodies beyond the Executive Committee) is not provided in the retrieved passages [Source 1].

Clear statement of the proportion of the Executive Committee’s total variable remuneration (or total remuneration) that is dependent on sustainability-related targets/impacts is not explicitly provided; only the share within the quantitative component is stated [Source 1].
Approval and update process for the terms of the incentive schemes (not just KPI values/benchmarks) and the level at which those terms are approved/updated is not described [Source 1].
For the long-term incentive, the full set of performance categories/metrics (beyond including sales carbon intensity reduction) is not disclosed in the retrieved passages [Source 1].
key_findings: ESG criteria are directly linked to annual variable remuneration for employees and the Executive Committee [Source 1].
Employees: ESG metrics account for 25% of total remuneration [Source 1].
Executive Committee: ESG metrics are 25% of the quantitative performance-based remuneration component (65%); this can increase based on strategic objectives [Source 1].

ESG KPIs/targets include energy transition (Scope 1&2 emissions and sales carbon intensity), safety (TRIR), and strategy execution milestones (including low-carbon projects and renewables portfolio execution) with stated weightings [Source 1].
KPI benchmark values are taken from business plans approved by the Board of Directors; performance is evaluated against actual results [Source 1].
Executive Committee long-term incentive is share-based with four-year vesting; share attribution includes reduction of sales carbon intensity as a criterion [Source 1].
